label: Other money for SF State students (rules checked 2026-10-01)
about: Every number the programs engine uses, with source and date. Code computes every value; the language model never does. A program whose value row is not valid today becomes 'check' (no dollars). Integers are whole dollars; strings are exact decimals (parse with Decimal, never float). Every amount is an estimate: each agency decides.

money.found_display_rule: sum of each counted line's display value

statuses.likely: shown with its yearly value; counted
statuses.check: shown with 'about $X if ...' or a range; never counted
statuses.zero: answered and worth $0 for this student; shown muted; not counted

list_only.rule: The status rules are read in order as in full mode and the first match decides; a 'hidden' result stays hidden and every other result becomes 'check' with no amount. No questions are asked.

evaluation_notes: Facts with a null value make the comparison false.
An 'lte_row' condition whose row is not valid today stops the status rules: the program becomes 'check' with no dollars.

A line whose status is likely, maybe or check and whose value row (value.row, fares_row, breaks_row or a tax row) is not valid today becomes 'check' with no dollars; a hidden, zero or note line is unchanged.
Outside 'effective' there is no programs part at all.

facts_defaults.text: ProgramFacts for slots the call never set: dorm_on_campus, homeless and roommates false; children_count 0; heat_cool false; other_utils 'none'; work-study and other income 0. A student who lives with roommates but never said how many is assumed to live with 2 (three people split the bill; the CARE line shows the assumption). An income the call never reached stays null. The CalFresh rules never read roommates_count.

calfresh_key.text: 12 x the monthly estimate, if your situation stays the same; the first month is prorated from the application day, so the real total can be a little lower

ask_rule.measure: spread(q) = max - min of found_yearly over q's choices, every other unanswered question held at 'unanswered'
ask_rule.note: a new yearly threshold for card questions; NOT voi.flip_threshold_usd, which is $50 of the monthly CalFresh amount (about $600 a year)

medi_cal.limit_138.rule: 138% of the 2026 HHS poverty guideline ($15,960 + $5,680 per extra person, 48 states) / 12, rounded up to the dollar as DHCS charts round (size 1: 15,960 x 1.38 / 12 = 1,835.40 -> 1,836; DHCS also showed 2025's 1,799.75 as 1,800). Effective 2026-01-01 for MAGI Medi-Cal per DHCS ACWDL 26-01 (the HHS page gives neither the date nor 138% values). The MAGI 5% disregard (about 143%) is not applied, so this limit is the conservative one.
medi_cal.limit_138.unverified: size 1 ($1,836) seen only in a search snippet of the DHCS chart (the page blocks automated reads); sizes 2-6 computed

medi_cal.limit_266_child.rule: 266% of the 2026 HHS guideline / 12, rounded up (MAGI children under 19)

clipper.fares.unverified: 2026 fares. The SFMTA budget approved 2026-04-21 ends the Clipper discount on 2027-01-04 (adult Clipper $3.00; monthly pass $90 in the proposal table), which covers about 15 of the 17 break weeks. Discount prices after that date are not confirmed (about $1.50 and $45 would give about $102 / $176 instead of $98 / $168). Keeping the 2026 fares makes the value a floor, not an overstatement. BART uses the system average fare.

clipper.breaks.unverified: Fall 2027 first day not published (summer gap end assumed 2027-08-18); whether Gator Pass starts on Jan 20 or Jan 25, 2027. 17 weeks is the low end of 17-18.6. The weekly-amortized pass ignores calendar months: a calendar-month estimate for Maria (single rides in partial months; the $43 vs $86 pass in June and July) gives about $200 instead of $168. For 2026-12-19 to 2026-12-31 the $43 pass is still the separate Lifeline sticker program, not part of START (START from 2027-01-01). Each of these makes the value conservative.

care.rates.unverified: the default bills ($140 two or more people, $100 alone) and the equal per-person share are assumptions (no official figure). The 70/30 split is not on any official page as such, but matches PG&E's typical bills in the 2026-03-01 advisories ($203.54 electric at 500 kWh + $86.54 gas at 31 therms = about 70% electric). 35% is the TOP of CPUC's 30-35% electric range; it is conservative only against PG&E's ~42% effective CARE discount at 500 kWh (electric advisory); with PG&E's own figures the blended saving is about 0.42 x 0.7 + 0.2 x 0.3 = 0.35, so 0.305 is conservative. The CARE base services charge (discounted to $6.00 a month, PG&E CARE page) is not modeled, so the real saving can differ either way.

lifeline.state.unverified: D.24-12-006 froze the amount from 2025-01-01 through 2026-12-31, or until a new SSA method is adopted, whichever comes first. The proposed decision in R.25-11-005 (mailed 2026-09-04; no legal effect until voted; earliest meeting 2026-09-17; adoption NOT confirmed) sets wireless Tiers 1-3 at $20.00 with $0 copay, effective on a date set by a CPUC Communications Division administrative letter (no fixed date); the wireline cap stays $19.00. The unfrozen formula would have given $27.50 for 2027 (PD Table 1), so $19 is a conservative floor either way. $19 is the Standard/Family wireless ceiling; the Basic tier is $12.85 (PD Table 2), and a plan that costs less than $19 saves less. The row still ends 2026-12-31 (then 'check') until the new amount and date are confirmed.

tax.caleitc_no_child_2025.label: about (2026 table not published; the tax-year-2025 table is a proxy)
tax.caleitc_no_child_2025.assumes: E = 12 x the monthly earnings said in the call, for all 12 months of 2026. The value is a credit amount, not a refund amount (the refund also depends on withholding).
tax.caleitc_no_child_2025.lookup: E between 6000 and 24000: the value at the smallest anchor >= E (the credit falls as E rises past $4,700, so this is a floor). E < 6000 or 24000 < E <= 32900: no counted state value (text 'plus a small state credit'). E > 32900: none.

tax.federal_eitc_2026.formula: floor(max(0, min(rate x E, max) - phaseout_rate x max(0, max(AGI, E) - phaseout_start))); AGI = E (no other taxable income modeled)

tax.yctc_2025.formula: E <= full_up_to: max; else floor(max x (zero_at - E) / (zero_at - full_up_to)), floor 0
tax.yctc_2025.label: about (2026 amount not published)

programs.counting_rule: GP-PROJECT policy, not a source rule: counted only at age 24+ with tax_dependent 'no' (student parents too). Under 24, a full-time student whose parent's home is still home (time away at school counts as living with the parent, Pub 596) is the parent's qualifying child and cannot claim EITC/CalEITC, even as a parent and even if the parent does not claim the EITC (exception: the parent is not required to file and files only to get withheld tax back). 'Lives with parents now' cannot decide this, so under 24 is always 'maybe'. CalEITC's own minimum age is 18 (FTB), so 24 is conservative.

value_models.flat_monthly: money.horizon_months x row.monthly, floored to the dollar; when row.ceiling is true the line is worded 'up to' (a cheaper plan saves less)
value_models.transit_breaks: rides = rides_per_week[answer]; weekdays_bart: floor(rides x bart_average_fare x start_discount x break_weeks). Muni: weekly_full = min(rides x muni_adult, muni_pass_month x months_per_year / weeks_per_year); weekly_start = min(rides x muni_start, lifeline_pass_month x months_per_year / weeks_per_year); value = floor((weekly_full - weekly_start) x break_weeks). Check range: lo = value(two_days), hi = value(weekdays_bart).
value_models.utility_share: B = default_bill_two_plus if people_in_home >= 2 else default_bill_alone; household = months x (electric_discount x electric_share_of_bill + gas_discount x (1 - electric_share_of_bill)) x B; value = floor(household / bill_split)
value_models.before_next_break: first gap whose (from - mail_days) >= today: apply_by = from - mail_days; none: null

'No Medi-Cal interview' and the BenefitsCal health-coverage screen names: search snippets only. Medi-Cal premium: $30 a month from 2027-07-01 for some adults by immigration status (ACWDL 25-33); whether the 2026-27 budget changed it is not confirmed. The card never says '$0 premium'.

Clipper START instant CalFresh verification right after a new approval, and whether the $43 Lifeline pass needs SF residency. Muni discount prices after the 2027-01-04 fare change are not confirmed; the 2026 fares are kept, so the Clipper values ($90-$440; Maria $168, about $200 by calendar month) are conservative.

PG&E: the default bill ($140 for two or more people, $100 alone), the equal per-person share and the 70/30 electric/gas split are assumptions (70/30 matches PG&E's typical bills in the 2026-03-01 advisories). The discount rates come from CPUC (30-35% electric, 20% gas) and PG&E (~42% electric effective, ~20% gas). The $6.00 CARE base services charge is not modeled. The account holder must not be someone's tax dependent and the home must not share a meter; neither is asked, so own_roommate stays likely only with the card note that says so.

LifeLine: D.24-12-006 froze $19 from 2025-01-01 through 2026-12-31, or until a new method is adopted. The 2026-09-04 proposed decision (R.25-11-005) sets wireless at $20 on a date a CPUC Communications Division letter will set; adoption is not confirmed. $19 is a ceiling (Basic tier $12.85). The provider list and the turnaround are not verified.

CalEITC and YCTC 2026 amounts are not published; the 2025 table is used as 'about' (a credit amount, not a refund amount). Earnings are assumed equal in all 12 months of 2026. F-1/J-1 CalEITC rules are not checked.
